payload.summary: The officer's report to the 5 March 2026 committee, written by the council's Regulatory Services Manager. It explains that the Licensing Act 2003 requires a policy to be reviewed at least every five years, that the current one was adopted by full council in December 2021, and that a replacement has to be in place by December 2026 or licensing decisions could be open to challenge. It recommends sending the draft to Cabinet for public consultation, and sets out who must legally be consulted, including the chief constable, the fire service and Norfolk's director of public health. It also gives the scale of licensing in the city: 677 premises licences, 9 club premises certificates, 1,963 personal licences, and 225 temporary event notices — the short-notice permissions used for one-off events — during 2025.
